title: Favorite pianists: Fats Pichon, Steve Lewis, Earl Hines, Fats Waller
summary: He names the pianists he liked, including Fats Pichon, Steve Lewis, Hines and Waller, who set the styles others followed.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Were there any favorite piano players down here? You had your mates like Earl Hines up there in Arkansas and all that time.

Oh yeah, well, his piano player that I liked around in New Orleans was Fats Pichon. I liked his playing until he was down there, worked with us down there by the Absinthe House. I was down there. I mean, after he went blind in there, I think that's about the best piano player I would've got. Well, my three was just him, and there was a piano player down here. He was pretty great too. Steve Lewis.
I was going to ask if you knew Steve Lewis. Yeah, he was a great piano player. I never got to know him.
He was a great piano player. Steve, Walter Pichon, all the guys that I met on the road, it was Oil Hines and Fats Waller.

Yeah. Now all the other guys came, I think, after those guys. They played styles, and they were similar to what they played. They had to build their own business for their business to build their business to build their and have a little freedom now to get around playing with different guys.
